title: Claude native refusals: match the CLI's real deny-rule/sandbox refusal texts or narrow the docs to the "requested permissions" refusal
outcome: TermAl's claims about which Claude CLI refusals end as bounded, abandoned errors match what it actually detects: every refusal text the CLI really emits for deny rules, its sandbox and managed policy either takes the refused-command path with a fixture proving it, or the docs and comments name only the refusal TermAl recognises.
acceptance: The Claude CLI's actual refusal texts for a deny rule, its sandbox and managed policy are recorded on the item from captured output or pinned upstream source, with locators.

Either is_permission_denial recognises each recorded text, with a behavioural fixture per text proving the command ends as an abandoned Error with a bounded reason and no approval card, or docs/architecture.md, the claude_native_denial test header and the claude.rs comments name only the refusal it recognises.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding and the full gate passes on the landing input.
